findings.title: Update benchmark probes to the current engine state layout
findings.why_it_matters: The visit-bound and candidate-set benchmarks never find the socket of a current daemon, so they time out rather than measure search behavior. The ranking candidate launcher makes the same mistake and can leave its spawned daemon running after reporting failure; the candidate-set probe also reads and writes a registry under the obsolete directory. These independent hard-coded layouts violate CODING_STANDARDS.md:10-13, which requires the state directory and home to be defined in one place and all layout checks updated on relocation.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the daemon socket and registry from the engine's configured state root and engine runtime directory, including 2BRAIN_HOME, instead of the tb-engine subdirectory; update the visit-bound, candidate-set, and ranking launchers together, and reap a spawned candidate on startup failure.

findings.title: Isolate the real-engine tests from configured state roots
findings.why_it_matters: When the caller has 2BRAIN_HOME configured, the real-engine suite starts its supposedly private daemon under that external state root, but waits only under its temporary HOME. Each test then waits until startup timeout instead of exercising the real engine, and its daemon can read the caller's registry. CODING_STANDARDS.md:10-13 requires the home of engine state to follow its single definition; replacing HOME without clearing or overriding 2BRAIN_HOME ignores that definition.
findings.suggested_fix: Set 2BRAIN_HOME to a fixture-owned path under the temporary home, or explicitly remove it, for every engine and MCP child in the real-engine fixture; test the suite with a nonempty inherited 2BRAIN_HOME.

findings.title: Use engine references for topic-map membership counts
findings.why_it_matters: The topic-map gap report counts every frontmatter wikilink to a map as a topic membership, including links from unrelated fields, so its missing-membership counts and --check result can be wrong. Its regex and filename-stem matching also bypass the engine's actual link resolution. CODING_STANDARDS.md:17-22 explicitly requires code needing engine state or a count to ask the engine rather than scrape files, and requires each metric to measure one defined thing.
findings.suggested_fix: Query the engine's resolved incoming references for each map, retain only topic-slot references, and compare those resolved member identities with resolved body references; add examples with an unrelated frontmatter link and an aliased or path-qualified link.
